paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus' word is enough. The official begged Jesus to come down to Capernaum, and Jesus never went. He said, "Go," and then, "Your son will live." The man "took Jesus at His word and departed" (John 4:50), and he walked home with nothing in his hands but a promise.

Think about how hard that walk must have been. I bet every step felt long, with his boy about to die (John 4:47) and no proof yet. Jesus had just said, "Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe" (John 4:48), and then this father believed before he saw a single thing. I think that's the part to hold onto, friend: trusting Jesus doesn't wait for the evidence to show up.

And then the evidence did show up, and it matched. The fever left at the very hour Jesus spoke, and "he and all his household believed" (John 4:53). So when you open the Word and it says something you can't see yet, take Jesus at His word like that father did. He is worth believing on the road, long before you reach the porch.
